2024_157_2_e_troyschools_scale3450df_014.paragraph: Price quote #014322, version 1, dated November 06, 2024, from People Driven Technology, Inc. to Troy School District for a Scale Computing 3450DF all-NVMe production cluster together with a three-year Veeam subscription. The cluster section subtotals $405,084.08 and the Veeam section subtotals $38,782.80, for a quoted total of $443,866.88. The largest components are five HC3450DF chassis at $41,633.84 each, extended to $208,169.20, and five-year SC//HyperCore 32-core standard licensing at $32,289.28 each, extended to $161,446.40. The quote is addressed to Alan Wilson at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 and carries an expiration date of 11/22/2024.

Both ship-to and bill-to addresses are Troy School District, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098.

Section one, titled 3450DF All NVMe Production Cluster, contains fifteen lines. Line 1: quantity 5 of part CHA-3-1F, HC3450DF chassis with Xeon SP CPU, 10x NVMe, 1U, including installation, at $41,633.84 each for an extended price of $208,169.20. Line 7: quantity 5 of HCOS-S-5-32C, five-year licenses and software for SC//HyperCore, 32C Standard, at $32,289.28 each, extended $161,446.40. The same support term, 1/30/2025-1/29/2030, is printed twice more in the header area of the line detail. Line 10: quantity 1 of MPVRR, VMware replace partner promo offer, at $0.00, extended $0.00. Clause 2, payment: payment is due net 30 days from invoice date unless otherwise specified, and any request to satisfy an invoiced payment by credit card or prepaid card vendor program is limited to $5,000 per invoice. Clause 3, delivery: products ship F.O.B. the customer's ship-to location set forth in the price quote, by a common carrier chosen by People Driven Technology, Inc. unless the customer instructs otherwise on its order letter.

Clause 4, shortage, claims and inspection: the customer may inspect products within 48 hours of receipt, and any shortage or other claim must be made in writing and delivered to People Driven Technology, Inc. within that 48-hour period or is waived. Clause 5, returns: the vendor has no obligation to accept returns, may at its sole discretion authorize the return of unused products, and no return may be made without a written return authorization. Clause 6, title and risk of loss: title and risk pass to the customer when products are tendered by each carrier at the customer's facilities, and the customer grants People Driven Technology, Inc. a purchase money security interest in the products and all proceeds from their sale until full payment is received. Clause 7, warranties and remedies: all products and their components are covered by the manufacturer's standard warranty, expressly in lieu of any other express or implied warranty by the vendor or manufacturer; the vendor warrants that services will be performed in accordance with the material specifications in the price quote and that the functions and features of the services and related deliverables will operate as described for ninety (90) days after completion. Clause 8, export restrictions: products may be subject to export or resale restrictions, statements as to country of origin, Export Control Classification Number, or legal compliance such as lead-free or RoHS status are as provided by suppliers, and the vendor does not warrant their accuracy. Clause 9, order cancellation: product cancellation or return is subject to manufacturer restrictions, up to and including a no cancellation or return policy. Clause 10, special notice: VMware pricing, part numbers and quote expiration dates may change at any time as a result of the Broadcom acquisition.

2024_160_m091724bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education held September 17, 2024 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, presented for approval at the October 15, 2024 meeting. President Karl Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt and Wilson present, Dr. Philippart absent, and roughly 75 members of the audience. The Board approved personnel recommendations covering 31 newly hired teachers, adopted a proclamation recognizing September 2024 as National Suicide Prevention Month, and authorized delegations to the MASB 2024 Delegate Assembly and to two 2025 NSBA conferences. All recorded votes were 6 yes, 0 no, with Philippart absent; the meeting adjourned at 8:51 p.m.
2024_160_m091724bdmtg.page:
Meeting and attendance
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, September 17, 2024, at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Present with him were Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt and Wilson; Dr. Philippart was absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators DiPilato, Pagel, Jansen, Haezebrouck, Griffor, Trudel and Milanov. Approximately 75 members of the audience attended. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary (GH/jh).

Recognitions
- Student representatives to the Board for 2024-2025: Kristian Vitanovich (Troy College and Career High School), Nurayda Albeez (International Academy - East), Diana D'Aloisio (Athens High School) and Adam McManus (Troy High School).
- All-State athletes for spring 2024, recognized by Mr. Jansen: Michelle Baik, Claire Balintfy, Ethan Bieniek, Louis D'Souza, Lauren DeJonckheere, Chase Duncan, Jacob Esser, Dylan Esser, Julian Farrell, Marin Fox, Jason Hamilton, Erin Humphrey, Olivia Jasniewicz, Nainka Jasti, Quinn Kelly, Hannah Lee, Michael Lim, Myles Linden, Nate Linden, Zach Macleish, Vishvaa Ravishankar, Kian Schneeweis, Nika Tananko, Sydney Taylor and Evan Watson.
- Student Spotlight: Thomas Butcher introduced Smith Middle School 7th graders Azra Yildiz and Seowoo Kim, recognized for work in the TSD Creative Guild.
- Michigan Association of School Boards awards presented by Dr. Machesky: Emina Alic and Matt Haupt, Certified Board Member Award and Award of Merit (all Level 1 courses and 45 education credits); Vital Anne, Master Board Member Award (Levels 1, 2 and 3 courses and a minimum of 368 education credits); Karl Schmidt, 12 years of service; Nancy Philippart, 16 years of service; and the TSD Board, Standard of Excellence Award.

Proclamation
On motion by Dr. Wilson, supported by Mrs. Anne, the Board adopted the Oakland Community Health Network proclamation recognizing September 2024 as National Suicide Prevention Month, citing World Suicide Prevention Day on September 10, CDC data that more than 48,000 people die by suicide each year, suicide as the second leading cause of death for ages 10 to 34, fourth for ages 35 to 54 and eighth for ages 55 to 64, and the work of NAMI and the 988 lifeline. Vote: 6 yes, 0 no, Philippart absent. Resolution adopted.

Section 1 update
Chris Bunch, Executive Director of Six Rivers Land Conservancy, updated the Board on the Section 1 Property, Turtle Woods Preserve, reporting that Oakland County Parks revised its new application and that the next Trust Fund Board meeting would be held in October.

Consent agenda
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mr. Haupt, approving items A through D: minutes of the August 20, 2024 Special Board Meeting, the August 20, 2024 Closed Session, and the August 20, 2024 Board of Education Meeting, plus the Treasurer's Report for July 2024. Vote 6-0, Philippart absent.

Personnel and curriculum
John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, reported on the hiring process and the factors driving annual teacher hiring, including retirements and resignations, full-year leaves of absence, FTE status and student enrollment; the District hired 31 new teachers this year. The personnel recommendations were approved on motion by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mr. Hauff, 6-0 with Philippart absent. Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching and Learning, presented on summer professional learning, including curriculum development, the UDL Conference, the administrative kick-off, the TSD Math and Literacy Project for the Pre-K Institute and Troy Institutes K-12, New Teacher Orientation and restorative practices.

Other business
No additions or deletions, no agenda-item public communication and no business items. Three community members addressed the Board during non-agenda public communication, with no action taken. The Board certified Matt Haupt, Gary Hauff, Nicole Wilson and Karl Schmidt as delegates to the MASB 2024 Delegate Assembly on October 24 at 7:00 p.m., with Nancy Philippart as alternate, and approved delegations of no more than four members to the 2025 NSBA Advocacy Institute in Washington, D.C. (February 2-4, 2025) and the 2025 NSBA Annual Conference in Atlanta (April 4-6, 2025). Meeting adjourned at 8:51 p.m.
2024_160_m091724bdmtg.verbose:
Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular board meeting held Tuesday, September 17, 2024 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, carried on the October 15, 2024 agenda for approval. President Karl Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt and Wilson were present; Dr. Philippart was absent. Superintendent Machesky attended along with administrators DiPilato, Pagel, Jansen, Haezebrouck, Griffor, Trudel and Milanov. Approximately 75 members of the audience were present. The minutes are signed Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typing notation GH/jh.

Recognition of student representatives. Mr. Schmidt introduced and welcomed the high school student representatives to the Board for the 2024-2025 school year. Kristian Vitanovich of Troy College and Career High School is a senior, AP student and student leader, a member of the TCC Student Council, a musician and songwriter active in the Music Club, and front man and lead guitarist of the TCC Rock House Band; he learned guitar one year earlier and has taken up cello and piano to advance his songwriting, and plans to attend college with aspirations of becoming a high school teacher. Nurayda Albeez of International Academy - East is a senior pursuing an IB Diploma, a member of the Superintendent Student Advisory Board since her freshman year and its president for the year, president of the IA Student Government, a former State Officer for the Michigan HOSA organization who facilitated statewide leadership conferences, and the recipient of the President's Volunteer Service Gold Award for three consecutive years after completing over 650 hours of community service; she is a former Barnard Bluejay and Baker Bobcat. Diana D'Aloisio of Athens High School is a senior scholar-athlete on the Athens Varsity Girls Golf Team, Vice President of the National Honor Society and a board member of the Athens Spanish Club, who plans to attend an in-state college and pursue a career in the medical field. Adam McManus of Troy High School is a senior serving as Student Government and Leadership Executive Board President, DECA Chapter President, Spanish Club President and a senior board member on the Principal-Student Advisory Board, and represents Troy High School and Oakland County on the Michigan Association of Student Councils and Honor Societies.

All-State athletes, spring 2024. Mr. Jansen and the Board recognized: Michelle Baik, senior, Troy High, girls' tennis; Claire Balintfy, senior, Athens, girls' lacrosse; Ethan Bieniek, freshman, Athens, boys' track; Louis D'Souza, senior, Troy High, boys' track; Lauren DeJonckheere, junior, Athens, girls' soccer; Chase Duncan, junior, Troy High, girls' lacrosse; Jacob Esser, senior, Athens, boys' track; Dylan Esser, senior, Athens, boys' track; Julian Farrell, junior, Athens, boys' track; Marin Fox, senior, Troy High, girls' tennis; Jason Hamilton, junior, Troy High, boys' track; Erin Humphrey, senior, Troy High, girls' lacrosse; Olivia Jasniewicz, sophomore, Troy High, girls' soccer; Nainka Jasti, sophomore, Troy High, girls' tennis; Quinn Kelly, junior, Troy High, boys' track; Hannah Lee, senior, Troy High, girls' tennis; Michael Lim, senior, Troy High, boys' lacrosse; Myles Linden, junior, Athens, boys' track; Nate Linden, sophomore, Athens, boys' track; Zach Macleish, junior, Troy High, boys' lacrosse; Vishvaa Ravishankar, senior, Troy High, boys' track; Kian Schneeweis, junior, Troy High, boys' track; Nika Tananko, senior, Troy High, girls' tennis; Sydney Taylor, senior, Troy High, girls' soccer; and Evan Watson, senior, Athens, boys' track.

Student Spotlight. The Board introduced the year's first Student Spotlight, which recognizes creative achievements in the TSD Creative Guild. Thomas Butcher was invited to the podium to introduce two 7th grade students from Smith Middle School, Azra Yildiz and Seowoo Kim, and to share their work.

National Suicide Prevention Month. Oakland Community Health Network asked school boards throughout Oakland County to partner with it by approving a proclamation designating September as National Suicide Prevention Month at their September board meetings. It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Anne to adopt the resolution, whose recitals note that September is known as National Suicide Prevention Month, that World Suicide Prevention Day is observed each year on September 10, that suicidal thoughts can affect anyone regardless of age, gender, race, orientation, income level, religion or background, that according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention each year more than 48,000 people died by suicide, that suicide is the second leading cause of death for people 10 to 34 years of age, the fourth leading cause among people 35 to 54 years of age and the eighth leading cause among people 55 to 64 years of age, that organizations such as the National Alliance on Mental Illness and the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, 988, work to help individuals in crisis, and that OCHN is committed to being a Zero Suicide organization. The resolved clause records that Oakland Community Health Network recognizes September 2024 as National Suicide Prevention Month and calls upon individuals, government agencies, public and private institutions, businesses, faith-based organizations and schools to recommit to increasing awareness and understanding of suicide prevention. Vote: yes 6, no 0, absent Philippart. Resolution adopted.

Michigan Association of School Boards awards. Dr. Machesky presented the Board with honors received during the past year. Trustees Emina Alic and Matt Haupt were recognized for the Certified Board Member Award and Award of Merit, requiring completion of all Level 1 courses and 45 education credits. Vital Anne was recognized for the Master Board Member Award, requiring completion of Levels 1, 2 and 3 courses and a minimum of 368 education credits. President Karl Schmidt was recognized for 12 years of dedicated service and Trustee Nancy Philippart for 16 years of dedicated service. The entire Board was congratulated for earning the Standard of Excellence Award, placing the Troy Board of Education among a handful of Michigan school district governing bodies demonstrating commitment to student achievement and exemplary leadership, with the minutes noting the Troy community is fortunate to have seven Board members committed to life-long learning and positive policy making.

Additions and deletions: none. Public communication on agenda items: none. Business: none.

Section 1 update. Mr. Chris Bunch, Executive Director for Six Rivers Land Conservancy, provided an update on the Section 1 Property, Turtle Woods Preserve. He indicated that Oakland County Parks revised their new application and that the next Trust Fund Board meeting will be held in October.

General consent agenda. Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C and D on the consent agenda: minutes of the August 20, 2024 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the August 20, 2024 Closed Session Meeting; minutes of the August 20, 2024 Board of Education Meeting; and the Treasurer's Report for July 2024. Vote: yes 6, no 0, absent Philippart.

Personnel, staffing update. John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, shared a report on the District's hiring process and the factors influencing the number of teachers hired each year, including retirements and resignations, full-year leaves of absence, FTE status and student enrollment. This year the District hired 31 new teachers. It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Hauff that the Board approve the personnel recommendations as stated. The new hires listed are Sara Abrin, Lauren Alarie, Hailey Ateek, Kelly Barker, Alyssa Baxendale, Benjamin Borglin, Britiany Bowers, Bradley Ciaramitaro, Isabella Contesti, Brittany Cwiertniewicz, Lillian DeLyon, Jenna Demeter, Riley Frazier, Heidi Haligowski, Lora Herbert, Tanille Hill, Madison Hutchins, Hannah Jackowicz, Steve Johansson, Monika Kitchen, Breanne Massie, Devron Minor, Alice Ochoa, Colleen Osis, Kirsten Paik, Stephanie Pindar, Shauna Pruess, Faith Pustover, Katie Schrepferman, Lauren Walkley and Kevin White. Vote: yes 6, no 0, absent Philippart.

Curriculum, summer learning. Director of Teaching and Learning Natalie Haezebrouck shared a PowerPoint presentation on the District's summer professional learning, covering summer curriculum development, participation at the UDL (Universal Design for Learning) Conference, the administrative kick-off meeting, and the TSD Math and Literacy Project for the Pre-K Institute and Troy Institutes K-12. She reported that New Teacher Orientation week went well and discussed restorative practices for building teams and future ready learning environments. Board members discussed the new calendar and their satisfaction that it is more culturally responsive; Ms. Haezebrouck noted that tool kits will be provided to help teachers respond to students and the diverse cultures in the school community. There was also discussion of the new furniture and the possibility of hosting job-embedded learning opportunities in buildings that have piloted it.

Public communication, non-agenda items. Three community members addressed the Board; no action was taken.

Reports from high school student representatives. Nurayda Albeez (International Academy - East), Kristian Vitanovich (Troy College and Career High School), Diana D'Aloisio (Athens High School) and Adam McManus (Troy High School) each reported on events and activities at their schools.

Other business. Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Anne that the Troy Board of Education certify Matt Haupt, Gary Hauff, Nicole Wilson and Karl Schmidt as delegates to the MASB 2024 Delegate Assembly on October 24 at 7:00 p.m., with Nancy Philippart as alternate. Vote: yes 6, no 0, absent Philippart. Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Alic that the Board approve a delegation of no more than four Board members as representatives at the 2025 NSBA Advocacy Institute in Washington, D.C., February 2-4, 2025. Vote: yes 6, no 0, absent Philippart. Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Board approve a delegation of no more than four Board members as representatives at the 2025 NSBA Annual Conference for Public Education Leaders in Atlanta, Georgia, April 4-6, 2025. Vote: yes 6, no 0, absent Philippart.

Board comments and adjournment. Board members welcomed new staff and welcomed everyone back to the start of the school year. Mr. Schmidt announced Coffee with the Board on Tuesday, October 8th from 6-7 p.m. at Hamilton Elementary School, the next Board Workshop on October 1st at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building, and the next regular meeting on October 15th in the Services Building at 7:00 p.m. The community was invited to attend the League of Women Voters' Meet the Candidate Forum on Wednesday, September 25th at 7:00 p.m. in the Troy School District Services Building. The meeting adjourned at 8:51 p.m.
